US 10Y trend in place of the INDOGB trend

ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

src: Yahoo Finance: IDX Composite (^JKSE) and USD/IDR (IDR=X) daily closes; any USD/IDR close more than 1.5% from Bank Indonesia’s JISDOR fix is replaced by JISDOR. INDOGB 10Y: PHEI IGSYC (CNBC benchmark 10Y before the first stored PHEI day). US Treasury daily par yields (2Y, 10Y; home.treasury.gov). Weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: USD/IDR 4-week % change (inverted: a weaker rupiah is bond-bearish)
INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 26-week average (wide = cheap)

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); spread vs its 130-day average; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; UST hedge β = trailing 130-day daily beta
components: INDOGB − UST 10Y spread vs its 130-day average (wide = cheap)

notes.headline: Treasuries jump 12bp but the 10Y INDOGB holds at 7.69% as the rupiah steadies at JISDOR 18,218 and the JCI rallies 1.8% on domestic buying; foreigners net sold stocks. The rebuilt daily signal is −0.76 and the sell-off episode since Sep 30 is +59bp. Signal −0.76: bond sell-off
notes.now: The JCI rose 1.78% to 5,344.41 and 5.82% on the week, yet foreigners net sold Rp229.8bn of stocks after Thursday's Rp443.5bn net buy, so the rally looks domestic; the rupiah firmed slightly, with JISDOR at 18,218 from Thursday's 18,241 record. Over 20 sessions the JCI is still down 11.97% and USD/IDR up 1.48% (the page's close, 18,149, is 0.4% below JISDOR, inside the 1.5% guard), so the month-long picture is still foreign money leaving Indonesian stocks; who traded bonds today is not published. The daily signal is −0.76 (−0.85 on Thursday after today's rebuild): the 10Y trend part is the most bearish (z +2.08, the 10Y up 59bp over 20 sessions), the JCI part z −1.21 and the rupiah part z +0.43, while the spread part (z +0.66) is the one bond-bullish input. INDOGBs pay 259bp over Treasuries, 17.4bp above the 130-day average and in the 75th percentile of 52 weeks, down from 271bp because the US 10Y rose about 12bp to 5.10% on Thursday; that is a nominal pick-up before currency risk. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.30 that US move implied +3.6bp for the INDOGB 10Y, which moved +0.2bp; the next-day spill-over beta is only 0.065, so little of it should carry into Monday. Over four weeks the US 10Y is unchanged, so with a 26-week weekly beta of −0.21 none of the INDOGB 10Y's +52.7bp is Treasury-linked: it is all residual, the part the US move does not explain, not proof of domestic selling or political risk. On the daily build the sell-off episode that began Sep 30 is still open, 21 sessions and +59.0bp. Since June 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.67 outright and 0.76 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 51% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 58%, hedged 64%) and the average 10Y move after a sell-off call was −1.7bp; these are in-sample back-tests. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: neutral on duration rather than short, because sell-off calls have had no edge and INDOGBs just shrugged off a Treasury sell-off; the rupiah and BI's Nov 17–18 decision remain the main risk, mostly to the 2–5Y.
notes.flip: The daily signal is in sell-off below −0.5 and sits at −0.76. A return to neutral needs the 10Y trend to cool as the late-October jump rolls out of the 20-session window, plus a JCI holding above 5,300 with the rupiah back near 18,050. A deeper sell-off would come from JISDOR moving past its 18,241 record, a JCI relapse below 4,900 or the 10Y above its 7.72% high. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound with foreign buying and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal; an orderly MPR choice of a new Vice President would remove the political trigger, a drawn-out one would sharpen it.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.

JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link; on the weekly build the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024), while the daily build did better over the same span.
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more. JCI −41% from its peak to about 5,344, 10Y up to 7.69%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners bid Rp18tn at the Nov 10 auction. Vice President Gibran resigned on Nov 12 and the rupiah hit a record low; on Nov 13 INDOGBs ignored a 12bp Treasury sell-off, and the daily signal stayed in sell-off (−0.76).
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money, and any statement about who bought or sold is a hypothesis. USD/IDR is Yahoo's close, replaced by Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fix on any day it strays more than 1.5% (Yahoo printed ~17,480 from Nov 3, 2026 while JISDOR was ~18,100); the 20-session windows count stored sessions, so gaps in the data stretch them and added sessions restate past signals. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The daily back-test runs from June 2022 (955 sessions): the live signal makes 179bp outright (Sharpe 0.67) and 201bp hedged against Treasuries (Sharpe 0.76), against −45bp for always holding the 10Y; the weekly build scores 0.35 and 0.44. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score up to 0.79 outright and 0.80 hedged on the weekly build but were picked after the fact and are not live. In-sample, no trading costs; not a trading system.
